EV051 and EV085 justify treating donor identity as a possible driver of catalyst stability, decomposition, or donor-derived confounding rather than assuming unchanged active species. EV004 and GX008 support paired operando or near-operando state tracking with catalytic time-course and rigorous controls. Proposed transfer: apply matched donor substitution within P01 and compare decay profiles and cobalt-state observables over time; this is a proposal, not a reported literature result for this exact mixtures for all groups using the literature-anchored component set; verify source-defined baseline composition where available and hold reactor geometry, gas handling, illumination program, and analytical workflow constant across groups.","Run photocatalysis under CO2 with repeated aliquot or headspace sampling at predefined time points; in parallel collect paired pre-reaction, during-reaction when feasible, and post-reaction cobalt-state measurements from matched samples for each donor condition.","Quantify CO and H2 at every time point and document whether signal grows, and state trajectories, then benchmark each against its no-cobalt control to exclude donor/support background behavior.","If operando acquisition is not feasible, use tightly timed near-operando freeze or rapid-transfer sampling validated by a pilot for minimal handling drift, and report conclusions as bounded by that limitation."],"measurements":["Time-resolved CO and H2 amounts from the same analytical method across all groups; these establish output and decay trends but not product origin by themselves.","Cobalt-centered state observables before, during, and after reaction using a transferable method such as XAS or another cobalt-sensitive spectroscopy; these can show donor-dependent valence or coordination changes but may not uniquely identify the active species.","Optional complementary UV-Vis, Raman, or IR signatures on matched samples to detect gross donor-dependent catalyst drift or new species; these are supportive only if assignments are validated.","Mass balance and visible precipitation or phase-change notes to flag catalyst loss or aggregation; these indicate persistence issues but cannot establish molecular identity.","No-cobalt control products and spectra to bound donor/support background contributions and prevent overassignment of donor-derived or support-derived signals to cobalt turnover."],"supports":"Support for H04 would be a reproducible donor-dependent difference between E21G01 and E21G02 in catalytic decay profile, cobalt persistence, or cobalt-state trajectory that is absent or much smaller in the no-cobalt controls. Stronger support is obtained if the donor giving different CO/H2 behavior also shows distinct cobalt-state drift or faster loss of cobalt-associated signal over time under otherwise matched conditions.","refutes":"H04 is weakened if E21G01 and E21G02 show similar time-dependent CO and H2 evolution, similar catalyst persistence, and no reproducible donor-dependent difference in cobalt-state observables beyond measurement uncertainty, while no-cobalt controls remain low and uninformative. It is further weakened if donor-dependent catalytic differences occur without any detectable difference in cobalt-state or persistence despite adequate sensitivity.","inconclusive":"Results are inconclusive if donor substitution changes multiple uncontrolled medium properties, if characterization sensitivity is insufficient to resolve cobalt under operating conditions, if no-cobalt controls show substantial donor-dependent background products or overlapping signals, or if only ex situ post-reaction differences are observed without validated linkage to the operating state.","parameter_selection":"Do not invent numeric settings. Use the source-anchored P01 formulation as the starting point and verify any missing concentrations, irradiation range, and sampling interval from the supplied source record before execution. Pilot rules: first confirm product signals are above blank and within the linear range of the product assay; choose time points dense enough to detect an early induction period, plateau, or decay; choose spectroscopic acquisition settings on concentrated matched samples or extended integration only after confirming that the method resolves cobalt above donor/support background; if operando signal is too weak, switch to a validated rapid-transfer near-operando workflow rather than claiming operating-state identity.","limitations":"Direct literature evidence for a strict TEA-versus-TEOA head-to-head in this exact P01 recipe is incomplete. The active cobalt species is unresolved, so state changes may remain descriptive rather than structurally unique. TEA and TEOA can alter donor strength, proton handling, CO2 interaction, viscosity, and coordination simultaneously, so even the primary contrast does not isolate a single causal subfactor. No-cobalt controls bound some background chemistry but do not recreate the full catalytic manifold. Post-reaction characterization alone cannot establish the true operating state.","feasibility":"moderate"}]}
